summary: Iteration 15 — GarmentImage / broken-image placeholder P0 fix. Verified 12 render sites now import and use GarmentImage (grep-audited). Playwright on mobile viewport (390x844) with seeded token → wardrobe browser correctly shows category-based clothing glyphs (hanger/sunglasses/diamond/shoe/tshirt) for all 5 null-photo seeded items (Cream linen blazer, Black tailored trousers, White cotton tee, Tan leather loafers, Gold hoop earrings) — NO broken-image icon, names + category still visible. Regression: seeded TEST_Real photo scarf (Accessories, 400x400 JPEG via /api/items) renders as a real element in the wardrobe grid (has_img=True). onError retry-once-then-placeholder path exercised via seeded TEST_Broken photo blazer (invalid base64) — console shows the expected 2 warnings ('photo failed to render, retrying once' → 'photo failed after retry, showing placeholder') and the UI falls back cleanly to the Outerwear hanger glyph. Home 'Recently added', Looks, Capsule, Planner, Packing, Shop, Profile, Stylist screens all load without any failed elements. ONE P0 BUG STILL PRESENT: /item/[id].tsx line 117-121 — when photos.length===0 the code still renders the generic Feather 'image' picture-frame glyph instead of the category placeholder, so opening a null-photo item (e.g. /item/item_bf79d6da50b3 Cream linen blazer) shows the exact broken-image-looking placeholder the PR was supposed to eliminate. The GarmentImage swap on line 114 only runs inside the photos.map(...) loop; the empty-photos else-branch was missed.

ui_bugs.issue: P0 acceptance criterion NOT met on Item Detail full-bleed gallery for null-photo items. Lines 117-121: `photos.length > 0 ? photos.map(<GarmentImage />) : <View><Feather name='image' size={40}/></View>`. For a null-photo item photos = [item.photo, item.worn_photo].filter(Boolean) = [], so the else branch renders a generic Feather 'image' picture-frame icon (looks like a broken/missing-image placeholder) instead of the category-based clothing glyph the PR promised. Reproduced by opening /item/item_bf79d6da50b3 (Cream linen blazer, Outerwear, null photo) — the gallery shows the picture-frame icon (see /tmp/item_null.png). Fix: replace the else branch with a single <GarmentImage photo={null} category={item.category} style={styles.galleryImg} iconSize={40} /> so the empty-photos state uses the same category-icon placeholder as every other render site. Same pattern check: /app/frontend/app/add-item.tsx L246 has a Feather 'image' placeholder in the duplicate-preview loop (`<View style={styles.dupImgEmpty}><Feather name='image'/></View>`) — should also use GarmentImage for consistency when a duplicate row has no photo (lower priority, only surfaces during native add flow).
ui_bugs.testID: item-detail-gallery (no explicit testID on the fallback View)

action_items: FIX (P0): app/item/[id].tsx L117-121 — replace the empty-photos else branch (`<View style={[styles.galleryImg, styles.placeholder]}><Feather name='image' .../></View>`) with `<GarmentImage photo={null} category={item.category} style={styles.galleryImg} iconSize={40} />` so null-photo items get the category clothing glyph instead of a generic picture-frame icon. This is the exact behaviour the GarmentImage PR promised on the Item Detail screen.

FIX (low): app/add-item.tsx L246 — for consistency, swap the `<Feather name='image'/>` dup-empty placeholder to a `<GarmentImage photo={null} category={d.category} style={styles.dupImg} />` (or at least a hanger icon). Not user-blocking; only visible during native add-item duplicate detection when a candidate has no photo.
Nice-to-have: add a testID (e.g. `item-detail-image-0`) to the GarmentImage inside item/[id].tsx gallery so future E2E tests can target the first gallery image without scanning by class.
critical_code_review_comments: GarmentImage component itself is well-written: useEffect resets `failures` on photo change (correctly handles item edit → new base64), single silent retry via recyclingKey key nudge, then placeholder at failures>=2, with warn-logs at each transition. Two console warnings + one final placeholder render matches the spec exactly, verified via playwright console capture.

12/12 render sites in the request list correctly import and use GarmentImage (grep confirmed): wardrobe.tsx L56, index.tsx L246, item/[id].tsx L114 & L255, dressme.tsx L219, stylist.tsx L219, looks.tsx L58, capsule.tsx L115 & L129, planner.tsx L145 & L197, packing.tsx L184 & L199, shop.tsx L172, profile.tsx L267 & L382. The ONLY leftover 'raw' item-photo placeholder is the item/[id].tsx L117-121 else branch (bug above) and the add-item.tsx L246 dup placeholder (secondary).

Other remaining `<Image source={{uri: data:image/...}}/>` sites are all NON wardrobe-item render paths and are fine as-is: bulk-add L126 (local pick thumb), looks.tsx L104 (o.preview_image is server-generated look PNG), tryon.tsx (user-captured person photo), add-item.tsx L188/L217 (local capture preview), shop.tsx L85 (uploaded shop check image). None of these render `items[].photo` from wardrobe items, so the P0 does not apply to them.

compress_b64 (server.py L640) normalises inbound base64 through PIL to bounded JPEG which produces clean, browser-decodable output for real-world photos (verified — 400x400 test JPEG round-tripped and rendered as an in the wardrobe grid). A pathological 1x1 hand-crafted JPEG can round-trip to something the browser refuses (net::ERR_INVALID_URL) — the GarmentImage retry+placeholder saved the UI in that case, which is exactly the graceful-degradation the component was built for.
MDI glyph mapping is comprehensive for the 8 categories the app uses; fallback of 'hanger' is a sensible default for any unmapped category (e.g. imported items without a category).

rca_of_issue: Item Detail gallery bug — RCA: The GarmentImage swap on item/[id].tsx L114 only covers the `photos.length > 0` branch. photos = [item.photo, item.worn_photo].filter(Boolean), so when both fields are null the array is empty and the ternary falls into the else on L117 which still renders the pre-fix `<Feather name='image' size={40} .../>` inside a plain View — exactly the generic picture-frame placeholder the PR was supposed to eliminate. Repro: (1) log in as user_testaura01, (2) tap any of the 5 null-photo seeded items in Wardrobe (e.g. Cream linen blazer), (3) observe the full-bleed gallery shows a mountain-in-a-frame icon rather than the Outerwear hanger glyph. Mitigation (single-line fix): replace the else branch with `<GarmentImage photo={null} category={item.category} style={styles.galleryImg} iconSize={40} />`. GarmentImage's showPlaceholder path handles photo===null gracefully (no fetch attempted, category glyph rendered immediately).
